>> Hi. Good evening, Mayor Dearinger and
City Council. Tonight's item is
consideration of a memorandum of
understanding to jointly fund a regional
drone program for the Los Angeles County
Sheriff's Department Lomita Station.
The program would serve Rolling Hills,
Rancho Palos Verdes,
Rolling Hills Estates, Lomita, and the
unincorporated parts of Palos Verdes
Peninsula.
It would provide LASD with a locally
available aerial resource for research
and rescue, mission Sorry, missing
person research
searches, disaster response,
suspect searches, and other critical
incidents. The program was developed
through the Regional Contract Law
Committee, which approved a
population-based cost cost-sharing
formula,
and directed each participating city to
consider the MOU.
This item was previously placed on our
agenda, but was removed after the MOU
went before the City of Rancho Palos
Verdes City Council, and additional
liability protections were requested.
Specifically, there was concern about
who would defend and indemnify the
participating cities if a drone were
used inappropriately and a lawsuit were
filed against both LASD and the cities
funding the program.
Staff delayed bringing the item forward
to ensure the liability language was
clarified and strengthened and fully
reviewed. The revised MOU has now been
reviewed both by the JPAA and city
attorney.
The revised language makes clear that
LASD will own the equipment and have
exclusive authority over its deployment,
operations, main- maintenance,
supervision, and use. The participating
cities will have no ownership interest,
operational responsibilities, or
liability for operating the drones.
The MOU does retain standard
indemnification language among the
participating cities. This means that
each city remains responsible for claims
arising from its own acts or omissions
related to the agreement itself. It does
not make Rolling Hills responsible for
another city's negligence or LASD's
operation of the drones.
This language is included to prevent
liability from being imposed on all
participating cities solely because
they're parties to the same agreement.
The city's potential acts or omissions
are extremely limited because our role
is essentially confined to contributing
our share
of the equipment costs and
administration
and administrating on our
our participation in the MOU.
All three of the other participating
cities have approved the MOU and the
proposed equipment package includes one
long-range drone, two daily use drones
for calls in service and incident
response, one interior drone for
tactical incidents, and the necessary
accessories to support
and support equipment. The total
equipment cost is $76,000.
Rolling Hills population-based share is
Future maintenance, repairs, and
replacement costs are estimated at
approximately 10% of each city's initial
contribution,
which would be approximately $152 for
Rolling Hills if such costs were
incurred.
After the first year, the cities will
review actual program usage and may
adjust the cost-sharing formula
accordingly.
For a relatively modest investment, the
city's participation would provide
Rolling Hills residents with access to
enhanced regional public safety
resource.
The recommendation is to approve the MOU
and authorize the mayor to sign the
agreement, and that concludes my report.
